signals.label: Early forefoot rocker
evidence: Adidas Adizero Adios Pro Evo 2 adds a higher forefoot stack, lower drop, and an early, sharply curved rocker favoring forefoot strikers.
Nike Alphafly 3 introduces a significant early‑stage rocker in the forefoot.
Nike Vaporfly 4 is a more aggressive design suited to shorter events with a lower stack height.
Vaporfly 4’s higher Flyplate angle and deep midsole channel increase the springboard effect.

signals.label: High stack 39–46 mm
evidence: Nike Alphafly 3 measured ~39 mm heel / 32 mm forefoot in independent testing.
Adidas Adios Pro 4 retains a near‑40/33 mm spec (RunRepeat lab measured 36.6/28.5 mm at WA points).
ASICS Superblast 2 lists ~45.5 mm heel / 37.5 mm forefoot stack.
ASICS Megablast measured ~44.6 mm heel / 35.9 mm forefoot on RTINGS’ bench.

signals.label: Woven/engineered mesh upper with internal bands
evidence: Adidas Adios Pro 4 uses a LIGHTLOCK woven mesh upper with internal locking bands and a thin racing tongue.
Nike Vaporfly 4 switches to a redesigned engineered mesh upper that helps cut weight.
ASICS Megablast features a super‑breathable mesh upper called out in reviewer testing.

signals.label: Zonal outsole rubber (mixed compounds)
evidence: Nike Alphafly 3 debuts a Fast Shot outsole for traction and grip with strategic coverage.
Adidas Adios Pro 4 uses LIGHTTRAXION rubber with a small Continental patch and generous coverage.
Adidas Adios Pro Evo 2 introduces a reimagined, grid‑like forefoot outsole pattern to add bite while saving weight.
ASICS Sonicblast employs ASICSGRIP rubber mapped to high‑wear zones for wet‑surface traction.

signals.label: Flared midsole base with raised sidewalls
evidence: Nike Alphafly 3’s heel flare and midsole sidewalls broaden the landing base and guide the foot forward.
ASICS Superblast 2 stabilizes its tall platform with foam sidewalls your foot sits within, plus a wide base.
RunRepeat lab notes Superblast 2’s sole flare extends beyond the upper to create a wider landing platform and added stability.

signals.label: Partial plate/rod systems in trainers
evidence: ASICS Sonicblast uses a 3/4‑length thermoplastic plate from midfoot into forefoot (plated super‑trainer).
RoadTrailRun confirms Sonicblast’s fiberglass/nylon plate paired with FF Turbo² superfoam.
Adidas Boston 13 is a plated super‑trainer using ENERGYRODS (glass‑fiber/carbon rods) rather than a full plate.
Doctors of Running’s quick eval of Boston 13 highlights the stiffer rods and lateral rod extension in a training‑oriented setup.

dossier.powershift: From hype-led icons to function-first essentials: stability runners, terrace-era trainers, trail-tech winterization, and hands‑free mules anchor commercial demand while runway heels/loafers swirl around them. ([vogue.com](https://www.vogue.com/article/is-the-reign-of-the-fashion-sneaker-over?utm_source=openai))
dossier.season_narrative:
FW26 arrives after 18–24 months of sneaker recalibration: runway coverage has leaned dressier while everyday wear keeps sneakers firmly in rotation. Street-style and retail signals show slimmer, hybrid silhouettes and “freakier” footwear drawing heat as classic hype cools. Vogue notes that fashion-sneaker searches have eased since the Samba’s April 2024 peak, and editors observed fewer sneakers on showgoers across recent fashion months; Highsnobiety’s FW26 recap echoed the shift toward loafers, brogues, and boots on the runway. ([vogue.com](https://www.vogue.com/article/is-the-reign-of-the-fashion-sneaker-over))

Within the sneaker space, terrace DNA hasn’t disappeared—it’s morphing. Adidas’ Q1 2025 results already showed lifestyle growth driven by Terrace/Skate/Retro Running franchises and flagged strong sell-out on low-profile “martial arts” lines (Taekwondo, Japan, Tokyo); 2026 coverage pushes that thread further with runway- and street-validated “sneakerina” and slim sport styles. Net-net, terrace goes beyond Samba into sleeker, ballet- and dojo-adjacent takes that keep price points accessible (KRW 150k–450k) and distribution broad. ([res.cloudinary.com](https://res.cloudinary.com/confirmed-web/image/upload/v1745902348/adidas-group/press-releases/2025/adidasAG_Q1_2025_Results_EN_Final_oa4skj.pdf))

Performance-rooted “stability” runners are now credible daily shoes. Nike formalized a simple three-pillar running lineup (Pegasus = responsive; Vomero = max cushion; Structure = supportive), clarifying benefits for both athletes and style adopters. Meanwhile ASICS’ SportStyle posted outsized growth in FY25 (+43.6% YoY) and accelerated again in Q1 FY26 (+69.6% YoY), powered by “vintage tech” icons (GEL‑1130/GT‑2160/Kayano 14) that read technical but style with tailoring. This is the most dependable commercial lane for FW26 in the contemporary tier. ([about.nike.com](https://about.nike.com/en/newsroom/releases/nike-road-running-footwear-lineup/))

Trail-to-city continues to broaden. Salomon’s XT family and similar lugged, speed-laced profiles have normalized in urban wardrobes, while fashion collabs (e.g., Cecilie Bahnsen x ASICS GEL‑Terrain MT) keep the aesthetic fresh. Editorial guides now style gorpcore sneakers as everyday polish rather than pure outdoors gear—evidence the category has shifted from microtrend to usable uniform. ([harpersbazaar.com](https://www.harpersbazaar.com/fashion/a60560078/salomon-sneakers/))

Slip-ons are a structural habit, not a summer blip. Retailers feature steady best-seller rankings for Nike Calm Slides/Mules, while clogs/sandals growth at Crocs and Birkenstock’s double‑digit constant‑currency gains through holiday 2025 signal durable demand for easy-on comfort across seasons—often at KRW ~60k–120k entry but scaling into suede/leather mules inside the 150k–450k band. ([hibbett.com](https://www.hibbett.com/shop/nike-calm-mule.html))

Put simply, FW26 is defined by four macros you can buy into now: STABILITY STYLE (supportive runners as everyday uniform), TERRACE REBOOT (slimmer, dojo/indoor-football updates to terrace icons), TRAIL CITY (technical trail DNA refined for town), and SLIP SHIFT (slides/mules/clogs normalize beyond summer). Each lanes into Nike/adidas/ASICS assortments with low execution risk and broad merchandising depth for FW26. ([fashionunited.com](https://fashionunited.com/news/fashion/retailers-and-trend-experts-share-footwear-trends-for-autumn-2026/2026040871633))

macrotrends.name: STABILITY STYLE
macrotrends.statement: Performance-stability trainers (ex: ASICS GEL‑KAYANO 33) and Y2K runners (ex: Nike Zoom Vomero 5) lock in lifestyle status for FW26, with metallic silver palettes amplifying visibility and shelf appeal.
macrotrends.narrative:
Across FW26, stability running icons and retro Y2K runners finish crossing over from performance to everyday wear. ASICS put fresh momentum behind the category by launching the GEL‑KAYANO 33 with new FLUIDSUPPORT stability and an engineered‑mesh upper positioned as softer and plusher—evidence that "stability" now reads as comfort-first in lifestyle, not just corrective tech. In parallel, Nike’s Zoom Vomero 5 line continues to expand with multiple 2026 drops in Grey Fog/Metallic Silver, Iron Grey/Chrome and White/“Aluminum” silvers, underscoring its wide uptake beyond running. ([corp.asics.com](https://corp.asics.com/en/press/article/the-new-gel-kayanotm-33-shoe-introduces-fluidsupporttm-technology-for-a-new-era-of-plush-stability-and-comfort?utm_source=openai))
Chrome-forward color stories accelerate the mood. 2026 consumer and editorial coverage repeatedly calls out silver sneakers as the year’s It shoe, while runway recaps cite metallic pairs styled at Simone Rocha, Prada and Dries Van Noten—validating “chrome runner” styling from high fashion down to mainline releases. Retailers even group dedicated “metallic silver sneakers” assortments, spanning Nike, New Balance and more, which helps concentrate demand. ([vogue.com](https://www.vogue.com/article/silver-sneakers?utm_source=openai))
Function-detail is part of the aesthetic: reflective accents, TPU heel cages and open‑mesh ventilation all read as design features and performance cues. Kayano 33’s mesh and guidance story, the Vomero 5’s molded cage and reflective make‑ups, and chrome‑synthetic overlays on adjacent Y2K runners (e.g., Nike P‑6000, NB ABZORB 2000) reinforce the look while keeping it practical for all‑day city wear. ([corp.asics.com](https://corp.asics.com/en/press/article/the-new-gel-kayanotm-33-shoe-introduces-fluidsupporttm-technology-for-a-new-era-of-plush-stability-and-comfort?utm_source=openai))

macrotrends.name: TERRACE REBOOT
macrotrends.statement: Post‑Samba mainstreaming: ’70s indoor silhouettes (adidas SL 72, Gazelle Indoor, Handball Spezial) carry the terrace look via refreshed variants, two‑tone suedes and broader rollouts.
macrotrends.narrative:
FW26 sees the terrace look evolve from Samba-driven hype to a diversified, mainstream lane anchored by adidas’ archive of indoor and lightweight runners. Press signals the pivot: in April 2024 The Guardian framed a “farewell” to Sambas and pointed to Gazelle, Spezial and SL 72 as the natural next step, while a Feb 2026 n‑tv.de trend brief for Germany states SL 72’s comeback and Handball Spezial’s rise, adding that Samba and Gazelle, though ever-present, are no longer the statement setters. ([theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/fashion/2024/apr/12/farewell-adidas-sambas-what-is-next-in-footwear?utm_source=openai))

Social/editorial buzz concentrates on SL 72 as the key “Samba alt.” British Vogue (June 2025) reported editors swapping in SL 72s at the office; adidas’ own Originals hub and product pages continue to spotlight SL 72 families (OG/RS/PT), with frequent sell‑through and restocks across regions, supporting everyday-wear adoption beyond niche fashion. ([vogue.co.uk](https://www.vogue.co.uk/article/adidas-sl72-trainers-trend?utm_source=openai))

Design codes update without leaving the hall: two‑tone suede packs and richer textures expand color language, while gum outsoles and T‑toes retain authenticity. 2026 releases include Handball Spezial “World Cup” two‑tone suede makeups and a Gazelle Indoor “Snakeskin” with metallic accents—proof that material/finish innovation is sustaining the category in FW26. ([soleretriever.com](https://www.soleretriever.com/news/articles/adidas-handball-spezial-world-cup-collection-release-date-march-2026?utm_source=openai))

macrotrends.name: TRAIL CITY
macrotrends.statement: Trail-tech sneakers and winterized runners cement themselves in city wardrobes: XT‑6 momentum, GORE‑TEX uppers, and hybrid hikers deliver cold‑weather utility with fashion credibility. ([s21.q4cdn.com](https://s21.q4cdn.com/769814866/files/doc_events/2026/02/1/Amer-Sports-4Q25-Management-Prepared-Remarks.pdf?utm_source=openai))
macrotrends.narrative:
- Built on the outdoor-to-urban flow of the past few years, Trail City marks a firm shift from niche gorpcore to mainstream footwear behavior. Salomon’s rise is emblematic: Amer Sports calls 2025 a breakout year with Salomon surpassing $2B in sales, and brand messaging now balances performance and sportstyle so the same shoes feel native on peaks and pavements. Fashion media reinforces the crossover; editorial roundups highlight the XT-6 as a go-to urban sneaker with functional credibility. ([s21.q4cdn.com](https://s21.q4cdn.com/769814866/files/doc_events/2026/02/1/Amer-Sports-4Q25-Management-Prepared-Remarks.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- The big sports players are doubling down on waterproofed, winter-ready sneakers that read like runners. Adidas Terrex Free Hiker 2 GTX is literally pitched for “forest floor to city streets,” while Nike’s ACG Mountain Fly 2 Low GORE‑TEX colorways repeatedly sell through across SNKRS and key retailers, and ASICS expands GTX across trail franchises including TRABUCO and SONOMA. Together, these validate hybrid hikers as a year‑round urban choice. ([adidas.com](https://www.adidas.com/us/terrex-free-hiker-2-gtx-climawarm-plus-hiking-shoes/KI8655.html))
- On runways and at fashion weeks, technical outdoor footwear keeps appearing—MM6 Maison Margiela’s ongoing Salomon collaboration and Moncler Grenoble’s alpine showings make rugged soles and performance uppers feel luxe, while seasonal color directions skew deep, mineral and winter‑bright per Pantone AW25/26. This is city utility with couture visibility. ([uk.fashionnetwork.com](https://uk.fashionnetwork.com/news/Mm6-maison-margiela-x-salomon-collaboration-expands-with-a-full-running-wardrobe%2C1720298.html?utm_source=openai))

macrotrends.name: SLIP SHIFT
macrotrends.statement: Hands‑free silhouettes scale for FW26: Nike’s Calm Mule meets adidas’s Adifom Stan Mule and ASICS’s GEL‑1130 Mule, while FW26 runways elevate the slipper from lounge to street.
macrotrends.narrative:
A new ‘hands‑free’ mood is redefining casual footwear as comfort tech crosses into street dressing. Foam‑molded mules like Nike Calm and adidas Adifom distill sneaker ease into sculptural, step‑in forms, while ASICS converts a retro runner into an open‑heel slip‑on. The look signals a broader shift toward frictionless entry and recovery‑inspired comfort worn all day. ([nike.com](https://www.nike.com/t/calm-womens-mules-zmUKYplJ/FB2186-502))
On foot, silhouettes read sleek and streamlined: one‑piece foam shells with subtle venting and removable straps; runner‑mule hybrids with mesh/synthetic uppers and GEL cushioning; and city slippers in leather, satin, or shearling. The effect is polished but effortless—closed toes and covered uppers make these viable beyond the house, pairing with denim, tailoring, and outerwear. ([nike.com](https://www.nike.com/t/calm-womens-mules-zmUKYplJ/FB2186-502))
Color follows FW26’s refined vibrancy: grounded neutrals and earths punctuated by saturated brights. Key picks from Pantone’s NYFW Autumn/Winter 2026/27 report—Muted Clay, Neptune Green, Green Envy, Arabian Spice, Foxglove, Festival Fuchsia, Red Mahogany, All Aboard, and Egret—map cleanly onto molded foams, quilted uppers, and smooth leathers for women, men, and kids. yearly_context.headline: Terrace diversifies and lifestyle runners surge; Samba halo shifts to SL72/Taekwondo as Retro Running gains.
yearly_context.what_changed: vs FW24: market — adidas footwear +17% YoY in Q1 2025 with Terrace/Skate/Retro Running leading; strong sell-out on Taekwondo/Japan/Tokyo (yoy_percent: 17; magnitude: strong; observed_note: adidas cites category mix and sell-through). ASICS SportStyle simultaneously inflects upward ahead of FW25 (yoy_percent: 43.6 FY25; magnitude: very strong).

yearly_context.headline: Runways begin to cool on statement sneakers; dressier shoes return as street keeps slim retro styles alive.
yearly_context.what_changed: vs SS25: shows — editors report fewer sneakers on showgoers and a dress-shoe tilt across fashion week; sneaker searches/visibility plateau relative to 2024 Samba peak (yoy_percent: null; magnitude: moderate; observed_note: FW25–SS26 cycle shows sneakers ceding lead aesthetic on runways).

yearly_context.headline: Slim hybrids (“sneakerina”), satin/sport crossovers, and terrace stalwarts (Gazelle/Samba) dominate street at shows.
yearly_context.what_changed: vs FW25: shows — Paris street-style highlights sporty retro (Gazelle/Samba) plus satin/ballet-influenced trainers; hybrid, low-profile shapes gain traction (yoy_percent: null; magnitude: strong; observed_note: 4 trainer trends at PFW include Sporty/Retro/Gorpcore).

yearly_context.headline: Four macros lock in: stability runners as daily shoes, terrace reboot via dojo/indoor-football cues, refined trail-tech, and normalized slip-ons.
yearly_context.what_changed: vs SS26: shows/market — retailers and forecasters call slimmer football/martial-arts influences; ASICS SportStyle accelerates in Q1 FY26 (+69.6% YoY) while adidas reports continued strong DTC sell-out trends (yoy_percent: 69.6 for ASICS SPS Q1 FY26; magnitude: big; observed_note: FW26 buy feedback favors tech runners, indoor heritage, and hybrids).

dossier.method_note: Method: triangulated public, citable signals across (1) market: brand IR/financial releases (adidas Q1 2025/2026; ASICS FY25/Q1 FY26; Crocs; Birkenstock) and live retailer rankings (Hibbett Nike Calm listings); (2) shows: Vogue/Highsnobiety runway and street-style reports, FashionUnited FW26 buy feedback; (3) consumer: Vogue’s reporting of Style Analytics search data on Samba decline; (4) trend indices: Lyst Q2 2025 confirming shoe dominance among hot products. All YoY figures are taken only where explicitly published; otherwise yoy_percent is treated as null and direction/magnitude rely on observable ranking, sell-through notes, and editorial consensus. Korean and English searches were used; outputs are in English.
open_questions: What share of the FW26 buy should shift from classic terrace (Samba/Gazelle) into slimmer dojo/football silhouettes (Taekwondo/Japan/Tokyo), and what is the exit plan if OG terrace demand drops faster than expected?
How deep should stability runners (Pegasus/Vomero/Structure; GEL‑1130/GT‑2160/Kayano 14) go in leather/suede fashion uppers to read “daily” while preserving run-specialist credibility?
Where is the optimal KRW price band per macro? e.g., STABILITY STYLE at 180k–260k KRW vs TERRACE REBOOT at 120k–190k, given wholesale and tariff pressure noted by brands.
How much trail tooling (lugs, speed-lace) will the city consumer accept in FW26 before the look reads too technical for office wear?
For SLIP SHIFT, should we prioritize winterized mules/clogs (shearling, rubberized) or clean foam silhouettes, given retailer data showing both volume and markdowns?
